newsitem.title: CHINA: China M2 up 19.1 percent at end-June - Xinhua.
newsitem.headline: China M2 up 19.1 percent at end-June - Xinhua.

text.p: China's broad M2 money supply was up 19.1 percent year-on-year at the end of June, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.
China's M1, or currency in circulation plus current business deposits, was up a year-on-year 20.6 percent at the end of June, Xinhua said.
M0, or currency in circulation, rose a year-on-year 19 percent at the end of June, it said.
Deposits at financial institutions around the country totalled 7,542.6 billion yuan ($908.7 billion) at the end of June, up 597.4 billion yuan from the beginning of this year, Xinhua said.
At the end of the first quarter, M2 was up 21.1 percent, while M1 was up 18.4 percent and M0 was up 13.6 percent.
The government has said it expects M2 to grow by 24.5 percent in 1997 and M1 by about 18 percent.
